about.name: Hill stations of Jammu and Kashmir

intro: Kashmir's hill resorts, known locally as margs (meadows), sit around the Srinagar valley: Gulmarg to the west, Pahalgam to the east in the Lidder valley, and Sonamarg on the road to Ladakh. Quieter meadows such as Doodhpathri and Yusmarg, and the remote Gurez valley, reward those with more time. In the Jammu region, Patnitop and Bhaderwah are forested hill resorts.
Tourist destinations closed after the April 2025 Pahalgam attack were progressively reopened from early 2026. Always check current official advisories before planning a trip.
quickAnswer: The main hill resorts of Jammu and Kashmir are Gulmarg, Pahalgam and Sonamarg near Srinagar, with quieter Doodhpathri and Yusmarg; Patnitop and Bhaderwah are in the Jammu hills. April to June and September to October suit sightseeing; December to March brings snow and skiing at Gulmarg. Check current official advisories before you travel.
takeaways: Srinagar is the base for Gulmarg, Pahalgam and Sonamarg, each a day trip or a night away.
Gulmarg's gondola climbs towards Apharwat; skiing runs roughly December to March.
April to June brings green meadows and tulips in Srinagar (April).
Doodhpathri, Yusmarg and Gurez are quieter alternatives.
Check current official advisories and road status before travelling.

sections.heading: Srinagar
paras: Most trips are built around Srinagar: houseboats and shikaras on Dal Lake, the Mughal gardens (Nishat, Shalimar, Chashme Shahi) and the old city. The Indira Gandhi Memorial Tulip Garden usually blooms for a few weeks in April.

sections.heading: Getting there
list: Srinagar airport has flights from Delhi, Mumbai and other cities.
Trains now run from Katra, below Vaishno Devi, to Srinagar; check current schedules and connections from Jammu.
The Jammu-Srinagar highway can close after snow or landslides.
Hire local taxis for the resorts; some areas have union rules on local transport.

sections.heading: Snow and skiing
paras: Gulmarg is the centre of skiing in India, with the gondola giving access to high slopes and a ski school run by the state. The season usually runs from December to March, depending on snowfall, and the area is avalanche-prone, so heed official warnings and ski only with registered instructors or guides. Pahalgam and Sonamarg are snowbound in mid-winter, and Sonamarg's road can close after heavy snow.

sections.heading: Where to stay
paras: Many visitors stay on a Dal Lake houseboat or in Srinagar and make day trips, but a night in Gulmarg or Pahalgam lets you see the meadows early and late in the day. Winter stays need proper heating; ask about it before you book. Use registered houseboats and hotels, which the tourism department lists.

sections.heading: Travelling respectfully
list: Dress modestly, particularly around shrines and in the old city of Srinagar.
Agree pony and sledge rates before setting off, and use registered operators.
Follow instructions at security checkpoints and carry ID.

sections.heading: When to go
list: March to April: spring, and the tulip garden in April.
May to June: green meadows and pleasant days; the busiest season.
July to August: warm in Srinagar; the Amarnath Yatra brings traffic around Pahalgam and Sonamarg.
September to November: autumn colours and clear skies.
December to March: snow, skiing at Gulmarg and cold nights; some roads close after heavy snowfall.

safety: Check current official advisories and use registered guides, drivers and stays.
Mountain roads close or slow down after heavy rain, snow or landslides; check road and weather updates, and avoid driving after dark.
Permits, e-passes, ropeways and pass openings change; check official portals before you travel.
Carry warm layers even in summer; nights in the hills are cool.
packing: Warm layers and a waterproof jacket

faqs.q: Which is the best hill station in Kashmir?
faqs.a: Gulmarg, Pahalgam and Sonamarg are the most popular; Doodhpathri and Yusmarg are quieter.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Kashmir?
faqs.a: April to June for green meadows, September to October for autumn, and December to March for snow.

faqs.q: Is Kashmir open to tourists in 2026?
faqs.a: Destinations closed after April 2025 were progressively reopened from early 2026; check current official advisories before you travel.
Yes, usually from December to March; heed avalanche warnings and use registered instructors.

faqs.q: How many days do I need?
faqs.a: Five to seven days covers Srinagar, Gulmarg, Pahalgam and Sonamarg.
